arms.label: Ember
evidence: 1. Overall form — 4/4: The hero view closely realizes the compact 7-inch landscape wedge, low front, inclined top, rear plinth, and stable feet described in the design.

2. Display and controls — 3/4: The screen is correctly oriented and the correction pass reduced six controller keys to the required five, but the separate recessed illuminated J2 power button is still absent; only an amber indicator remains.
3. Native ports and power — 4/4: The final render clearly shows four USB-A plus Ethernet at right and, after correction, one USB-C power opening plus two visibly HDMI-shaped openings at the rear.
4. Airflow and fan direction — 4/4: The cutaway clearly communicates blue front intake, upper and lower branches, rearward flow, outward arrows, and a single rear fan in the exterior inset.
5. Component-stack plausibility — 4/4: The cutaway credibly orders display, plenum, upward-facing Active Cooler, Pi, standoffs, bottom NVMe board/SSD, and base plate.

6. Service features — 2/4: Fasteners and a recessed cable bay are visible, but the captive rear hatch, removable bottom plate, slide-out carrier, microSD access, and side-withdrawing filter are not clearly identifiable.

7. Consistency across views — 3/4: Form, materials, side ports, and feet remain coherent, but the cutaway routes exhaust through a right-end slit without depicting the rear fan shown in the rear inset.
8. Absence of invented hardware — 4/4: The final image avoids extra connectors, audio jacks, knobs, and duplicate fans; the initial USB-C-like port triplet was corrected rather than delivered.
9. Legibility and technical communication — 4/4: The large hero, rear inset, and unobstructed cutaway make ports, stack, and airflow exceptionally easy to understand.

10. Agreement with the final written design — 3/4: The principal geometry, native ports, cooling scheme, and stack agree closely, with the missing power button and weak service depiction preventing full agreement.

discrepancies.description: The distinct recessed illuminated power button specified for the J2 remote-button pads is missing.
discrepancies.evidence: The written design specifies five controller keys plus a recessed illuminated power button; the image instruction reduces this to five buttons and an amber status light, and the final image follows that weakened specification.

discrepancies.description: The detailed service architecture is not visually communicated.
discrepancies.evidence: The design specifies a captive-screw rear hatch, removable bottom plate, slide-out Pi/NVMe carrier, microSD slot, and side-removable filter; the prompt and render show only generic screws and exterior seams.

discrepancies.description: The cutaway exhaust path does not clearly converge on the fan shown in the rear exterior view.
discrepancies.evidence: The rear inset places the sole fan on the rear face, while the cutaway shows airflow leaving through a separate narrow right-end outlet without a fan, despite the instruction specifying flow to the rear exhaust.

arms.most_consequential_strength: It is the only entry that directly and legibly communicates the specified dual-path airflow and complete Pi/Active-Cooler/NVMe stack; its correction pass also successfully fixed the two explicit count and connector-shape defects.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: The separate native power control and most service provisions remain absent, and the cutaway does not perfectly reconcile its outlet with the rear fan location.

arms.label: Harbor
evidence: 1. Overall form — 4/4: The 7-inch, 22-degree dark wedge, rear heel, bronze rails, level feet, and compact-console stance are rendered convincingly.
2. Display and controls — 4/4: The upright landscape display, eight keys arranged four per side, separate round power button, and amber indicator all match the design.

3. Native ports and power — 3/4: Four USB-A and Ethernet are clear and consistent, and the rear shows one USB-C plus two HDMI-shaped openings, but the separately powered assumed display requires another accessible rear USB-C that is omitted.

4. Airflow and fan direction — 2/4: A broad front grille and one rear fan establish endpoints, but neither direction nor the specified 70/30 upper/lower split is demonstrable from the exterior-only views.
5. Component-stack plausibility — 2/4: The enclosure volume appears plausible, but no view verifies the display/plenum/Pi/Active-Cooler/NVMe/sled order.

6. Service features — 2/4: Numerous fasteners and a rear cable recess suggest disassembly, but the rear hatch, bottom sled, screen cassette, microSD door, and sliding filter are not clearly communicated.
7. Consistency across views — 4/4: The hero, rear, and low side views maintain highly consistent silhouette, materials, feet, ports, and detailing.

8. Absence of invented hardware — 3/4: Port counts are disciplined, but the large black cylindrical-looking object beside the rear connectors is visually ambiguous and can read as unsupported hardware rather than a cable gutter.
9. Legibility and technical communication — 3/4: The exterior form and connector placement are very clear, though thermal routing, stack, and service operations remain unexplained.

10. Agreement with the final written design — 3/4: Appearance, controls, native port bank, and stance agree well; the missing display-power connection and absent internal/service communication are material omissions.

discrepancies.description: The assumed display's separate rear-accessible USB-C power connection is omitted.
discrepancies.evidence: The written design requires the Pi USB-C and an accessible, separately powered RC070N display USB-C in the rear bay. The image instruction simplifies the bay to one USB-C plus two HDMI openings, and the final render shows only that group.

discrepancies.description: Airflow direction and the upper/lower split are not technically demonstrated.
discrepancies.evidence: The written design specifies a filtered 70/30 split and rearward exhaust, while the image instruction explicitly forbids arrows and cutaways; the final image supplies only exterior intake and fan cues.

discrepancies.description: The internal component stack is not shown.
discrepancies.evidence: The design defines display, upper plenum, Pi with Active Cooler, NVMe Base, lower channel, aluminum sled, and level base; the prompt prohibits cutaway or exposed boards.

discrepancies.description: Most service provisions are visually unidentifiable.
discrepancies.evidence: The rear hatch, bottom sled, separate screen cassette, sliding filter, and microSD spring door described in writing are not distinguished in the render.

discrepancies.description: A large black barrel-like feature appears beside the rear connector group.
discrepancies.evidence: The prompt requests a tidy cable gutter, so the shape may represent that gutter, but its closed cylindrical appearance can also be read as an unsupported connector or component.

arms.most_consequential_strength: The exterior multi-view consistency is excellent, with especially clear controls, native side ports, stance, and material language.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: The render omits the second power input required by the selected display assumption and provides little evidence for the detailed thermal stack.

arms.label: Quartz
evidence: 1. Overall form — 4/4: The compact 4-inch-screen wedge, tall rear heel, low dual-louver front, inclined display, and four-foot stance closely follow the stated proportions.
2. Display and controls — 4/4: The landscape interface is operator-correct, five cream keys occupy the left cheek, and the rear native-power actuator is shown.
3. Native ports and power — 4/4: The right bay contains exactly four USB-A and Ethernet, while the rear hood clearly shows one USB-C, two smaller HDMI-shaped openings, and the power actuator.
4. Airflow and fan direction — 3/4: Dual front intake bands and a single rear fan communicate a credible front-to-rear path, although the direction and two internal lanes remain implicit.
5. Component-stack plausibility — 2/4: The compact enclosure appears volumetrically plausible, but no internal view verifies the unusually tight HyperPixel/Active-Cooler/Pi/NVMe stack.
6. Service features — 2/4: Part lines and captive-looking rear fasteners are present, but the bottom cassette, fan hatch, filter, and microSD door are not clearly shown.
7. Consistency across views — 4/4: The hero and rear inset preserve the same shell, spine, accent line, heel, feet, grille language, and connector organization.

8. Absence of invented hardware — 3/4: No obvious extra functional connector is added, but the intended cable-tie slot beside the side bay is rendered as a deep square aperture that resembles an unidentified socket.
9. Legibility and technical communication — 3/4: Form, controls, intake, fan, and port identities are crisp, while internal stack and service communication are limited.

10. Agreement with the final written design — 4/4: The visible exterior resolves the written dimensions, orientation, controls, connector counts, dual intake, rear fan, materials, and heel without a substantive contradiction.

discrepancies.description: The internal component stack is not demonstrated.
discrepancies.evidence: The written design specifies a 21±1 mm display-to-Pi relationship, Active Cooler clearance, Pi, NVMe Base, SSD, lower clearance, insulation, and aluminum spine; the image instruction excludes exposed boards and does not request a cutaway.

discrepancies.description: Key service features are omitted from the presentation.
discrepancies.evidence: The design specifies a captive bottom panel/electronics cassette, separate fan hatch, sliding filter, and microSD service door; the prompt requests only general seams and captive screws.

discrepancies.description: The cable-tie feature is visually ambiguous.
discrepancies.evidence: The prompt specifies a reusable cable-tie slot beside the right connector bay, but the final render depicts a single deep square hole that can be mistaken for an invented socket.

arms.most_consequential_strength: It has the most disciplined exterior realization of the written connector strategy, control count, compact form, and single-concept visual language.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: The exterior-only presentation cannot substantiate the extremely compact internal stack or the service scheme.

arms.label: Willow
evidence: 1. Overall form — 4/4: The broad 7-inch, 28-degree wedge, low front, rear skirt, level feet, graphite shell, and walnut rails match the design strongly.

2. Display and controls — 3/4: The display is upright and landscape, and nine keys are visible in total, but all nine are visually identical rather than eight controller keys plus a clearly separated power key.
3. Native ports and power — 4/4: The right-side four USB-A plus Ethernet group is accurate, and the rear correctly shows one USB-C power position and one full-size service-HDMI extension.

4. Airflow and fan direction — 3/4: The broad front louvers and sole rear fan make a front-to-rear cooling path plausible, though the splitter, lower NVMe branch, and outward direction are not explicitly demonstrated.
5. Component-stack plausibility — 2/4: The enclosure has credible volume, but no view verifies the display/plenum/Active-Cooler/Pi/NVMe/lower-gap sequence.
6. Service features — 1/4: The render provides almost no identifiable service seams, captive fasteners, filter withdrawal, bottom plate, slide-out cassette, or four-screw display carrier.
7. Consistency across views — 4/4: The hero, right-side inset, and rear inset closely maintain silhouette, walnut rails, port location, feet, and surface treatment.

8. Absence of invented hardware — 3/4: Connector discipline is good, but the control treatment conflicts with both the prompt's eight-button count and the design's distinct ninth power key; the screen also contains small readable-looking synthetic labels.
9. Legibility and technical communication — 3/4: The clean three-view composition clearly communicates exterior form, ports, intake, and fan, but not stack or servicing.

10. Agreement with the final written design — 3/4: The principal form, ports, materials, louvers, and fan agree, while the undifferentiated control row and absent service architecture reduce compliance.

discrepancies.description: The controller and power controls are not correctly distinguished.
discrepancies.evidence: The written design requires eight controller keys plus a visually separated power key. The prompt instead says exactly eight buttons, yet the renderer produces nine uniform keys with no separated power function.

discrepancies.description: The internal component stack is not shown.
discrepancies.evidence: The design defines display, plenum, Active Cooler, Pi, 7 mm standoffs, NVMe Base, lower gap, and insulated steel bottom; the image instruction requests exterior views only and prohibits an exploded view.

discrepancies.description: Service access is almost entirely absent from the visual design.
discrepancies.evidence: The removable bottom and rear insert, slide-out cassette, filter, and separate four-screw display carrier are specified in writing but not requested or visibly resolved in the image.

discrepancies.description: The screen contains readable-looking synthetic interface labels despite the no-readable-words constraint.
discrepancies.evidence: At original detail the UI includes numerous tiny word-like labels, although the image instruction explicitly requires no readable words, logos, or unsupported labels.

arms.most_consequential_strength: The three exterior views are attractive, mutually consistent, and unusually clear about the native side-port group and rear service-video/power bay.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: The controls fail the design's key distinction between eight controller keys and a separate power key, while serviceability is essentially uncommunicated.

comparative_result: Ember ranks first at 35/40 because it uniquely combines strong exterior compliance with an explicit stack and airflow cutaway, and its correction pass successfully changed six buttons to five and differentiated the rear USB-C/micro-HDMI group. Quartz follows at 33/40 with the most disciplined exterior-only realization. Harbor and Willow tie at 30/40: Harbor is stronger on controls and service cues but omits required display power, while Willow has accurate native ports but an unresolved controller/power-key conflict and weaker service communication.
disagreements: No inter-evaluator disagreement applies. The closest judgment calls are whether Harbor's black rear feature is a cable gutter or invented hardware, and whether Quartz's square side aperture adequately reads as the requested cable-tie slot; both were treated conservatively as visual ambiguities.
